# Feature: Browser Widget Observability & Step Efficiency

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-009
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)
**Predecessor**: FEAT-FP-007 (`feature_agent_grounding.md`) introduced `browser_form_fill`, `UrlProvenance`, and the uncapped internal resolution this spec builds on.

An agentic `do` run must be able to drive the ordinary interactive widgets of a real
booking/search site — a searchable destination box, a two-panel date calendar — in roughly
the number of steps a human would take, and must be able to tell what state the page is
actually in while doing it.

Diagnostic baseline, run `20260806T013327Z-do-dec13852` (goal: _"find some cheap hotels near
frisco, texas for 8/6/2026 to 8/8/2026 in expedia site"_): **67 turns, 459s wall clock, 96k
tokens, $0.24** — and the run still published prices for the wrong date range (Aug 6–7
instead of Aug 6–8) because the agent never succeeded in selecting a check-out date. A human
does this in four clicks.

Target after this feature: the same goal completes with the correct dates in ≲25 turns.

### Root causes established from the run artifacts

| #   | Cause                                                                                                   | Evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A   | Two different accessible-name implementations exist; the observation path uses the weaker one           | `interactable-scan.ts:108` restricts its text-content tier to `'button,a,[role="option"],[role="menuitem"],[role="tab"]'` — omitting `[role="button"]`/`[role="link"]`. Expedia day cells carry `role="button"` on a non-`<button>` tag → `name: ""`. `trace.json` steps 27/30/40/54 record the **same clicked elements** as `{"role":"button","name":"1"}` / `"2"` / `"5"` / `"3"` via the locator engine's Playwright-port name algorithm. |
| B   | Ranking by `rect.top` alone interleaves side-by-side calendar panels, and the 30-cap truncates mid-grid | `observe.ts:76-79`. Expedia renders August and September panels side by side → same-row cells share `top`. 19 of 30 slots went to header chrome, leaving 11 cells straddling both months. Positional proof: `e424`=Aug 1 (disabled), `e425`=Sep 1 → click set "Sep 1 – Sep 2"; later `e518` (6th of 11) → Sep 5. The model spent 8 attempts reverse-engineering this mapping and never succeeded.                                            |
| C   | `bestNameMatch` cannot match a bare day number                                                          | `browser-form-fill.ts:380`. Given `"2026-08-06"` it tries exact / `"August 6, 2026"` / month+day-loose / prefix / substring. A cell named `"6"` misses every tier → `FORM_WIDGET_NO_MATCH` (twice in the run). With two panels there are also _two_ cells named `"6"`, so bare-number matching needs month context to be safe.                                                                                                               |
| D   | `disabled` is computed but dropped before the model sees it                                             | `interactable-scan.ts:57` computes it and `rankInteractables` emits it for deterministic discovery, but `AgentInteractable` is `{ref, role, name}`. Four calls died on `ELEMENT_DISABLED`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| E   | No current value or selection state is exposed                                                          | `AgentInteractable` never carried them. This is **not** a privacy decision — every model-visible payload already passes `maskUserInputDeep` → profile sanitizer → byte cap at `middleware.ts:615-632`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| F   | `URL_NOT_FROM_EVIDENCE` refuses a query-value variant of an already-visited URL                         | The model reasoned correctly and was blocked: _"The current URL has `d1=2026-08-06&…&d2=2026-08-07`. If I could change `d2` and `endDate` to `2026-08-08`…"_. `browser_navigate` then refused `/Hotel-Search` (seq 102) even though that exact path had been visited with a query.                                                                                                                                                           |
| G   | Every action costs two round trips, and each observation re-ships an unchanged 8KB digest               | 25 of 67 calls were `browser_observe`; actions return only `{url, title}`. Tool execution accounted for ~130s of the 459s — the rest was model time over oversized, low-signal payloads.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## 2. Technical Context

> Standing rules (coding standards, architecture, testing, logging, security) are in
> `.spec-lite/memory.md` and are unchanged by this feature.

### Approach

**One accessible-name algorithm, not two.** The locator engine already ships a correct
Playwright-port implementation (`locator/injected/role.ts`, reached through the injected
`window.__yantra` bundle). Rather than patching the scanner's heuristic a second time, expose
a cheap `describeAccessible(element) → { role, name }` on the injected API — reusing `getRole`
and `getElementAccessibleName`, and deliberately **skipping** `describeElement`'s CSS/XPath
candidate ranking, which is far too expensive to run over 400 elements — and have
`scanInteractablesInPage` prefer it.

**The scanner keeps its own `computeRole`.** `agent-controller.ts:298-317` records that the two
role maps deliberately differ (`<select>` → `combobox` for the scanner vs `listbox` for the
engine; `input[type=search]` → `textbox` vs `searchbox`). `browser_form_fill`'s role switch,
`kindByRole`, and the protocol's `InteractableDescriptor.kind` enum are all written against the
scanner's map. Adopting the engine's roles is a separate change with its own blast radius and
no bearing on the reported bug, so this feature takes the engine's **name only** and files the
role question in `TODO.md`.

**Graceful degradation is mandatory.** When the injected bundle is unavailable (a test double
with no `locatorHost`, a cross-origin frame, a page mid-navigation), the scanner falls back to
its existing `computeName` — which is itself repaired to include `[role="button"]`/`[role="link"]`
in its text tier. No path regresses relative to today.

**Widget scope beats viewport position.** When a modal, popover, listbox, or grid is open, that
is where a human is looking. Elements inside an open overlay are ranked ahead of page chrome,
and within a scope the sort key becomes `(top, left)` rather than `top` alone — which by itself
de-interleaves side-by-side calendar panels. Each element carries the accessible name (or first
heading) of its nearest labelled container as `group`, giving `"August 2026"` vs `"September 2026"`
and making a cell named `"6"` unambiguous.

**Value exposure rides the existing chokepoint.** `middleware.ts:615-632` already masks vault
values back to their `{{user:…}}` tokens and runs the profile sanitizer over the whole payload,
so an added `value` field inherits both. The one protection the sanitizer cannot provide is
never reading a password or one-time-code field at all — that is enforced in-page, before the
value leaves the browser.

**URL provenance relaxes on values, never on shape.** `UrlProvenance` gains an
`origin+path → seen query keys` index. A candidate is allowed when its origin and path match a
visited URL _and_ its query keys are a subset of the keys seen at that origin+path. `d2=2026-08-08`
passes; the fabricated `c17823` city id that motivated the class — whether as a new path segment
(`/hotels/Chicago,IL-c17823/…`) or a new parameter (`cityId=c17823`) — is still refused.

**Efficiency is three independent, individually revertible changes**: actions return their
post-action observation; unchanged digests are replaced by a `digest_unchanged` flag; and the
prompt/error text stops nudging the model toward the loops it fell into.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

- **`PROMPT_VERSION` bump is required, not optional.** `prompt.ts:14-25` states that any
  semantic change to `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` requires a version bump so persisted prompt hashes
  stay interpretable. TASK-008 changes the trust-boundary sentence, so `agent-v6` → `agent-v7`.
- **The agent's interactable cap diverges from the protocol's.** `DEFAULT_INTERACTABLE_CAP`
  (agent-controller.ts) rises 30 → 50 so a full month grid plus the surrounding form fits in one
  observation. `MAX_INTERACTABLES` in `discovery/interactables.ts` stays at 30 — it is bound by
  the `DiscoveryObservation` Zod schema and governs the separate deterministic discovery path.
- No other overrides — see memory.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

No persistent schema changes. `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist and none is introduced.
The in-memory observation record is extended:

### Entities & Attributes

- **`RawInteractable`** (`packages/core/src/discovery/interactable-scan.ts`) — in-page scan record, never model-visible as-is:
  - `role` (string) — unchanged; from the scanner's own `computeRole`
  - `name` (string | null) — **now** from `__yantra.describeAccessible().name` when available, else `computeName`
  - `kind` (`'button'|'link'|'input'|'select'`) — unchanged
  - `disabled` (boolean) — unchanged
  - `top` (number), `visible` (boolean), `selectorIndex` (number?) — unchanged
  - `left` (number) — **new**; viewport-relative left edge, secondary sort key
  - `group` (string | null) — **new**; accessible name (or first heading text) of the nearest labelled container, ≤80 chars
  - `scope` (`'dialog' | 'page'`) — **new**; `'dialog'` when inside a visible open overlay
  - `value` (string | null) — **new**; current text/selection, ≤120 chars, `null` when absent or withheld
  - `valuePresent` (boolean) — **new**; `true` when a value exists but was withheld (password/OTP)
  - `checked` (boolean | null) — **new**; checkbox/radio state
  - `expanded` (boolean | null) — **new**; `aria-expanded`
  - `selected` (boolean | null) — **new**; `aria-selected` or `aria-current`

- **`AgentInteractable`** (`packages/core/src/browser/agent-controller.ts`) — the model-visible projection:
  - `ref` (string), `role` (string), `name` (string) — unchanged
  - `group` (string) — **new**, emitted only when non-empty
  - `disabled` (true) — **new**, emitted only when true
  - `value` (string) — **new**, emitted only when present
  - `value_present` (true) — **new**, emitted only when a value was withheld
  - `checked` / `expanded` / `selected` (boolean) — **new**, each emitted only when non-null

  > Falsey and null fields are **omitted**, not emitted as `false`/`null`. With a 50-element
  > cap, emitting eight always-present keys per element would cost more payload than the
  > digest suppression in TASK-007 saves.

- **`AgentBrowserObservation`**:
  - `url`, `title`, `interactables` — unchanged
  - `digest` (string) — **now** `''` when unchanged since the previous observation of the same document
  - `digestUnchanged` (boolean) — **new**

### Relationships

- One `AgentBrowserObservation` has N `AgentInteractable`, ordered by `(scope, top, left)`.
- Each `AgentInteractable` belongs to at most one `group` (a plain string label, not an entity).

### Indexes & Constraints

- `UrlProvenance` gains `queryKeysByOriginPath: Map<string, Set<string>>` keyed by
  `${scheme}//${host}${path}` (path normalized exactly as `parse()` already does).
- `AgentBrowserController` gains `lastDigestHash: string | null`, cleared on navigation commit
  alongside `refs` and `refIdByIdentity`.

    Take that container's accessible name (`aria-label`, then `aria-labelledby`, then `<caption>`
    for a table). **If the container has no accessible name, fall back to the text of its first
    descendant heading** (`h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6,[role="heading"]`) — this is what yields
    `"August 2026"` on Expedia, whose month panels carry a heading rather than a label. Normalize
    whitespace and truncate to 80 chars; return `null` when nothing is found.

    `[role="dialog"], [role="alertdialog"], [aria-modal="true"], dialog[open], [role="listbox"], [role="menu"], [role="grid"]`

### TASK-003: Expose disabled, current value, and selection state

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Extend `RawInteractable` with `value: string | null`, `valuePresent: boolean`,
    `checked: boolean | null`, `expanded: boolean | null`, `selected: boolean | null`.
  - In-page value read:
    - `HTMLInputElement` / `HTMLTextAreaElement` → `.value`
    - `HTMLSelectElement` → the selected option's `label || text`
    - `[contenteditable]` → `textContent`
    - anything else → `null`
    - Normalize whitespace, truncate to 120 chars.
  - **Withholding rule, enforced in-page before the value ever leaves the browser** — return
    `{ value: null, valuePresent: <raw length > 0> }` when any of:
    - `element.matches('input[type="password"]')`
    - the element's `autocomplete` attribute matches
      `/\b(current-password|new-password|one-time-code|cc-number|cc-csc|cc-exp)\b/i`
    - `element.hasAttribute('data-yantra-secret')`
  - `checked` from `HTMLInputElement.checked` for `checkbox`/`radio`, else `aria-checked`, else `null`.
  - `expanded` from `aria-expanded` (`'true'`/`'false'`), else `null`.
  - `selected` from `aria-selected`, else `aria-current` when not `'false'`, else `null`.
  - Project onto `AgentInteractable` as `value`, `value_present`, `checked`, `expanded`,
    `selected`, plus `disabled` — **each omitted entirely when false/null/empty**.

### TASK-004: Calendar-aware field matching, month paging, and post-fill verification

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - `bestNameMatch(candidates, value)` — add a **day-cell tier**, placed after the existing
    ISO-date loose tier and before the prefix tier. When `value` parses as an ISO date:
    1. `dayCells = named.filter(c => /^\d{1,2}$/.test(c.name.trim()) && Number(c.name.trim()) === date.getUTCDate())`
    2. Narrow to cells whose `group` contains the long month name (case-insensitive); if the group
       also contains a 4-digit year, require it to equal the target year.
    3. Return the single survivor, or `null` when 0 or >1 remain. **Never guess** — picking one of
       two same-numbered cells is exactly the failure that produced "Sep 5" for "Aug 6".
  - `chooseInWidget` — after opening the widget and failing to match, add bounded month paging:
    - Locate a `Next month` / `Previous month` control by name (case-insensitive, allowing
      `Next`/`Previous` alone) among the observed interactables.
    - Choose the direction by comparing the target `year-month` against the months named in the
      observed `group` values; when no group parses as a month, default to forward.
    - Click, re-observe uncapped, re-run `bestNameMatch`; repeat to at most `MAX_MONTH_PAGES = 12`.
    - Stop early and report when the paging control is `disabled` (the run hit the widget's bound).
  - `chooseInWidget` — after a successful cell click, re-resolve the **trigger** element (by its
    original ref, falling back to its original name) and read its current `name` + `value` into a
    new `AppliedField.resulting_value` field, so the model sees `Dates → "Thu, Aug 6 - Sat, Aug 8"`
    in the same tool result rather than discovering three turns later that it picked the wrong month.
  - New typed failure `FORM_WIDGET_NO_EFFECT` (`retryable: true`) when the click landed but the
    trigger's rendered value is byte-identical to what it was before the click, carrying the
    observed value in `details`.
  - `FORM_WIDGET_NO_MATCH` message — render candidates as `"name" (group)` pairs instead of bare
    names, and state the paging bound when paging was attempted and exhausted.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - `bestNameMatch([{name:'6',group:'August 2026'},{name:'6',group:'September 2026'}], '2026-08-06')`
    → the August cell.
  - Same candidates with `'2026-09-06'` → the September cell.
  - Candidates with two `"6"` cells and **no** group → `null` (ambiguous, never a guess).
  - A cell named `"6"` whose group is `'August 2025'` with target `2026-08-06` → `null` (year mismatch).
  - Existing tiers are untouched: `"August 6, 2026"` still matches exactly; a plain textual value
    still resolves by prefix/substring.
  - `chooseInWidget` with a fake controller whose first observation shows September and whose
    `Next month` click advances to October: paging stops at `MAX_MONTH_PAGES` and returns

### TASK-005: Relax URL provenance to query-value variants

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Extend `ParsedUrl` with `originPath: string` (`${scheme}//${host}${path}`, path normalized by
    the existing rule) and `queryKeys: readonly string[]` (from `parsed.searchParams.keys()`).
  - Add `private readonly queryKeysByOriginPath = new Map<string, Set<string>>()`. `record()`
    creates the entry for every recorded URL — **including query-less URLs, which register an
    empty set** — and unions in the URL's query keys.
  - In `has()`, after the existing exact-match and origin-root checks, add: look up
    `queryKeysByOriginPath.get(parsed.originPath)`; when present, return `true` iff every one of
    the candidate's query keys is in that set. This makes a bare `/Hotel-Search` reachable after
    visiting `/Hotel-Search?destination=…` (empty key set ⊆ anything), which is the exact seq-102
    refusal in the logged run.
  - Update `browser-navigate.ts`'s refusal message so a blocked model knows what _is_ allowed:
    name that query **values** of an already-visited URL may be varied, but a new path or a new
    parameter name may not, and point at `web_search` / clicking through for anything else.
  - Update the module doc's closing paragraph, which currently states the rule "will not treat a
    _different_ query string as the same URL" — that is no longer accurate.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Record `https://x.test/Hotel-Search?destination=Frisco&d1=2026-08-06&d2=2026-08-07`, then:
    - `…?destination=Frisco&d1=2026-08-06&d2=2026-08-08` → allowed (value varied)
    - `…?destination=Frisco&d1=2026-08-06` → allowed (key subset)
    - `https://x.test/Hotel-Search` → allowed (empty subset)
    - `…?destination=Frisco&cityId=c17823` → **refused** (new key)
    - `https://x.test/hotels/Chicago,IL-c17823/2026-08-05` → **refused** (new path)
    - `https://y.test/Hotel-Search?destination=Frisco` → **refused** (different origin)
  - Recording a query-less `https://x.test/a` does **not** subsequently allow `https://x.test/a?q=1`.
  - Keys accumulate across records: after recording `?a=1` and `?b=2` at the same origin+path,
    `?a=9&b=9` is allowed but `?a=9&c=9` is refused.

### TASK-007: Suppress unchanged page digests

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Add `private lastDigestHash: string | null = null` to `AgentBrowserController`.
  - In `observe()`, hash the freshly built digest with
    `createHash('sha256').update(digest).digest('hex').slice(0, 16)`. When it equals
    `lastDigestHash`, return `{ ...snapshot, digest: '', digestUnchanged: true }`; otherwise store
    the hash and return `digestUnchanged: false`.
  - Clear `lastDigestHash` in the `onNavigationCommitted` callback in `installPagePolicies`,
    beside `invalidateObservation()` and `refIdByIdentity.clear()` — a new document must always
    ship its digest.
  - Clear it in `performTeardown` too.
  - Project as `digest_unchanged: true` with the `digest` key **omitted** when unchanged.
  - Internal uncapped observations (`observe({ cap })` from `browser_form_fill`) must **not**
    update `lastDigestHash` — they are never shown to the model, so letting them consume the
    "already sent" state would silently suppress a digest the model has genuinely not seen. Gate
    the hash update on the call being the model-visible one (add an internal
    `{ trackDigest?: boolean }` option defaulting to `true`, passed `false` by the resolution-cap
    callers).
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Two consecutive `observe()` calls on an unchanged page: the first carries the digest, the
    second carries `digestUnchanged: true` and an empty digest.
  - A digest change between calls → the second carries the new digest and `digestUnchanged: false`.
  - After a simulated navigation commit, the next `observe()` carries the digest even when the
    text is byte-identical to the pre-navigation page.
  - `observe({ cap: 400 })` does not update the tracked hash: an internal observation followed by
    a model-visible one still yields a full digest.
  - The projection omits the `digest` key entirely (rather than sending `""`) when unchanged.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: `docs/agent-tools.md` — document `digest_unchanged` and point at
      `browser_extract` with `kind: 'content'` as the way to re-read page text on demand. JSDoc on
      `observe()` covering the tracking rule and why internal observations are exempt.

  goal before and after; expect a material reduction driven by the repeated marketing boilerplate
  no longer being re-sent on every observation.
- **Depends on**: TASK-006

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: No change. `browser_form_fill` still refuses credential-shaped values via
  `SECRET_SHAPE` and remains credential-free; `browser_fill` with `secret_ref` remains the sole
  credentialed path, and `assertHostBinding` / `withSecret` / the consent flow are untouched.
  TASK-003 _adds_ protection by refusing to read password and one-time-code fields at all.
- **Error Handling**: Every new failure is a typed `DomainFailure` with an explicit `retryable`
  flag and a message that names the next useful action — `FORM_WIDGET_NO_EFFECT` (retryable),
  the reworded `URL_NOT_FROM_EVIDENCE` (retryable), and the paging-exhausted variant of
  `FORM_WIDGET_NO_MATCH` (retryable). Best-effort paths degrade rather than throw: injection
  failure falls back to the local name heuristic, and a post-action observation failure omits the
  observation instead of failing the action. Month paging is hard-bounded at 12 iterations, and the
  existing `trackFailureStreak` breaker in `orchestrator.ts` still keys on `${tool}:${errorCode}`,
  so a repeated `FORM_WIDGET_NO_MATCH` still trips the stuck-loop breaker.
- **Logging**: No new log statements carry element values. `tool-calls.jsonl` records the
  already-sanitized model payload, so exposed values arrive there having passed
  `maskUserInputDeep` and the profile sanitizer; password and OTP values never enter the process
  at all. The promoted-workflow trace continues to record fill values in masked form
  (`services.userInput.mask(...)`) and is not touched by this feature.
- **Security**: The privacy posture is _strengthened_ on the value question (in-page refusal for
  credential fields, on top of the existing chokepoint) and _deliberately relaxed_ on the URL
  question in a bounded way — origin, path, and parameter **names** must all still be attested by
  a real tool result, so the fabricated-identifier failure the rule was written for remains
  refused. The known `web_fetch` provenance gap is unchanged by this feature and remains tracked
  in `TODO.md`.
